title: Add Postgres logical-replica migration hook and Helm preflight checks
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Private installs often require schema migrations across large customer datasets. Existing migration tooling in the installer relied on single-node offline migrations or ad-hoc scripts which caused lengthy maintenance windows for customers with large Postgres datasets. This PR introduces a Helm-chart-level, optional logical-replication-based migration flow plus preflight checks so operators can perform zero-downtime schema/application upgrades in the private installer. What this changes: 1) new chart values (values.yaml additions) to opt-in to logical replica migration: enableLogicalReplicaMigration, migrationReplicaImage, replicationSlotConfig, replicationLagThresholdSeconds, migrationCheckpointBucket, perTenantDryRunLabel. 2) a new pre-upgrade Helm preflight hook (kind: Job) that validates target chart values, ensures required K8s permissions and checks connectivity to the configured checkpoint storage (S3/GCS) and target primary Postgres via a short connectivity & permissions probe. If any preflight fails the Helm upgrade is blocked. 3) a migration-controller Job template (post-upgrade hook) that triggers logical replication setup: it provisions a temporary logical replica pod (from migrationReplicaImage), creates a replication slot on the primary via pg_create_logical_replication_slot, subscribes, and streams WAL until the migration validation job asserts schema compatibility. 4) a migration-checkpointer sidecar that writes checkpoint tokens (timestamp + WAL LSN) to the configured checkpoint bucket periodically; this allows safe resume/rollback and avoids replaying WAL from the beginning on retry. 5) operators can perform a dry-run per-tenant by setting the perTenantDryRunLabel on tenant k8s resource; dry-runs simulate schema changes using the replica and report a per-tenant impact score. 6) detailed chart notes and example commands added to NOTES.txt for operators. Implementation details: - preflight job templates include explicit rbac rules (create jobs, get secrets, list PVCs) and fail with clear errors to surface missing cluster privileges. - the replication job contains a configurable lag-check loop that waits until replication lag is below replicationLagThresholdSeconds before proceeding to schema assertions. - checkpointing uses a simple JSON token format written to s3://<bucket>/migrations/<cluster>/<migration-id>.checkpoint to make resume logic idempotent. - migration manifests are stored in a new ConfigMap name: redwood-migration-manifest-<migration-id> and are immutable once applied; the chart will refuse to run a conflicting migration-id to prevent accidental double-runs. - rollback path: if the migration assertion fails, the post-upgrade hook will automatically stop the replica, remove the replication slot when safe, and surface a human-readable failure summary with the most recent checkpoint location to restore from. - observability: new Prometheus metrics (migration_progress_seconds, replication_lag_seconds, checkpoint_writes_total) and structured logs for audit. Testing and validation: - unit/helm-lint checks added. - integration: a Kind-based e2e job runs a small primary+replica pair and performs a synthetic schema change to validate the dry-run path. - manual internal test: ran on a 3TB dataset snapshot with a representative schema; replication catch-up and checkpointing validated. Rollout plan: default is disabled. Operators must opt-in via chart values and provide a migrationCheckpointBucket and migrationRole ARN/credentials. We will enable as a staged opt-in for private customers and document procedure in the private-installer runbook (linked in Linear ticket). Backwards compatibility and safety: the features are fully opt-in and do not change any default manifests. The immutable migration-id check and checkpoint tokens are designed to prevent accidental re-application. Related work: builds on ENG-2248 (migration orchestration), complements existing backup/restore playbooks (SUP-1982).

review_comments: Liam O'Neill: Overall this is great work — two requests: (1) add clearer logs for checkpoint write failures so operators can retry without digging through S3 history, (2) can we make the replicationLagThresholdSeconds per-tenant overrideable?

Maya Chen (author): Added more detailed checkpoint error handling and exponential backoff; made replicationLagThresholdSeconds overridable via tenant annotations in the migration job template. Pushed fix in c4f5d12.

Priya Kapoor: Please ensure the preflight job fails fast when credentials for checkpoint bucket are invalid instead of timing out the whole helm upgrade. Also add a migration-id validation regex to avoid path traversal in checkpoint keys.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented fast-fail check for bucket credentials and added regex validation for migration-id (only alphanumeric, dash, underscore). Added unit tests to cover validation.
Daniel Rivera: Approving pending small nit in NOTES.txt about recommended IAM roles. Verified e2e logs show replication_lag_seconds stable under threshold in the synthetic workset.
merge_commit_message:
Add logical-replica migration flow and Helm preflight checks (Maya Chen)

Opt-in logical replication migration: preflight validations, migration replica job, checkpointing, immutable migration manifests, observability and operator notes.

Linked: ENG-2248, SUP-1982
release_notes: Optional logical-replica migration flow for private deployments (helm opt-in). Adds preflight checks, migration replica job, checkpointing, and immutable migration manifests. Disabled by default.
notes_for_ops: Enable by setting charts.redwood.enableLogicalReplicaMigration=true and provide charts.redwood.migrationCheckpointBucket and credentials. Use helm upgrade --set charts.redwood.migrationId=<id> --install ... The migration will run as a post-upgrade hook and write checkpoints to <bucket>/migrations/<cluster>/<migration-id>.checkpoint. To resume supply the same migrationId and ensure checkpoint access. For dry-run add perTenantDryRunLabel=<label> to tenant resource metadata.
post_merge_actions: Backfill docs in private-runbooks and schedule a migration playbook review with SRE and customer-ops. Notify pilot customers via dedicated rollout channel.
notes: This PR targets private-installer customers that require near-zero downtime schema changes. Because it introduces opt-in IAM/credential requirements, the rollout will be gated by an enable flag and a short internal training for customer success and SRE teams.
